Apex Industrial Equipment - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Industrial Equipment Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question during the Q&A session, please press star then 1 on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Industrial Equipment's results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are John Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to John Ramirez.

John Ramirez (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Apex Industrial Equipment's performance for the third quarter. We've made significant progress on several fronts amid a dynamic industrial landscape. We delivered solid market share gains in key high-growth segments, effectively navigating macroeconomic headwinds affecting end-market demand. Operating margins expanded across our segments through favorable mix and productivity. We've made strong strides in resolving supply chain constraints. Order intake remained robust with healthy book-to-bill ratios by end market. We're providing clear operating margin guidance for Q4 and the full year, and we continue to execute on our shareholder-friendly dividend policy.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Turning to our financial performance, Apex Industrial Equipment reported $2.85 billion in revenue for the third quarter, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 44.5%, driven by pricing discipline, favorable product mix toward automation and services, and productivity gains from our digital initiatives. Operating expenses were $1.05 billion, reflecting targeted investments in R&D and supply chain resilience, resulting in operating income of $550 million. Our net income for the quarter was $420 million, or $1.92 per diluted share.

We are committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet, with $1.2 billion in liquidity and robust free cash flow generation exceeding 95% conversion.

As we dive deeper into our Q3 results, I'd like to spend some time on our market share performance across key markets—a critical leading indicator for our long-term growth in the industrial equipment space. Overall, we delivered solid share gains in high-growth segments, offsetting some softness in cyclical end-markets, resulting in a net global market share expansion of 150 basis points year-over-year to 14.2% in our core $45 billion total addressable market for precision machining and automation systems. This marks our third consecutive quarter of sequential gains, driven by our TechStack 3.0 platform rollout and targeted capacity expansions.

Let me break this down by key end-markets, where we're leveraging our strengths in CNC machining centers, collaborative robots, or cobots, and electro-hydraulic presses.

Starting with automotive, which represents 32% of our revenue: We gained 220 basis points to 18.5% share, outpacing peers like Haas and DMG Mori. This was fueled by strong demand for EV battery assembly lines and lightweighting equipment for aluminum chassis. Our new ApexFlex EV Press series, with 25% higher throughput and integrated inline quality inspection via AI-driven vision systems, secured $250 million in orders from North American OEMs like GM and Ford. Average selling prices held firm at $1.2 million per unit, up 8% year-over-year, as customers prioritize our superior overall equipment effectiveness ratings—now averaging 92% versus the industry benchmark of 85%.

In aerospace and defense, 22% of revenue, we experienced a modest 50 basis point share loss to 12.8%, primarily due to aggressive pricing from European incumbents like Siemens and MTU Aero Engines amid Boeing's production ramp challenges. That said, our market position stabilized in Q3 with wins on F-35 supply chain tooling, where our high-precision 5-axis CNCs delivered mean time between failures exceeding 5,000 hours. We're countering this with a $150 million capital expenditure commitment to our South Carolina facility for AS9100-certified composites machining.

Semiconductor equipment, our fastest-growing vertical at 15% of revenue, saw explosive 350 basis point gains to 11.2% share—closing the gap on leaders like Applied Materials. The CHIPS Act-fueled fab expansions in the U.S. and Europe played to our strengths: Our QuantumEtch plasma etching systems captured 20% of new wafer fab orders, with deployments at TSMC's Arizona site and Intel's Ohio greenfield. Our technical edge includes proprietary cryogenic cooling technology, reducing defect rates by 40% and enabling 2nm node compatibility.

Renewables and heavy industrials, 18% of revenue, delivered flat-to-up share at 16.1%, with gains in wind turbine nacelle gearboxes offsetting softness in solar tracker hydraulics. Key win: A $180 million frame agreement with Vestas for our high-torque gear hobbing machines, emphasizing our sustainability credentials—our equipment cuts energy use by 30% via variable frequency drives.

Finally, general industrials, 13% of revenue, saw a 100 basis point erosion to 13.4%, hit by destocking in consumer electronics assembly amid China's economic slowdown. We're addressing this through cobot retrofits, where our ApexBot AR series gained traction with small and medium-sized businesses seeking plug-and-play automation.

Geographically, North America drove 60% of our share gains, expanding to 22.3% plus 180 basis points, propelled by reshoring trends—U.S. manufacturing capital expenditure hit $220 billion annualized, per recent ISM data. Europe held steady at 11.5% minus 20 basis points, pressured by the energy crisis and German auto slowdowns, but our UK battery gigafactory wins with Nissan mitigated losses.

Asia-Pacific was mixed: China share dipped 80 basis points to 9.8% on weak EV demand and local competition from Foxconn, but we offset with 400 basis point gains in India to 7.2%, securing Reliance Industries' orders for petrochemical presses. Japan remains challenged at 10.1% minus 150 basis points, as Fanuc dominates robotics, but our joint ventures there are yielding dividends in precision grinding.

These dynamics reflect our disciplined playbook: 12% of revenue reinvested in R&D, yielding 15 new SKUs this year, including IoT-enabled predictive maintenance that boosts customer uptime by 18%. We've also accelerated mergers and acquisitions, closing the $400 million acquisition of RoboForge last month to bolt on advanced welding tech for e-mobility.

Looking forward, we see 200-300 basis points of additional share upside in fiscal 2025 from our $1.2 billion capacity ramp—adding 25% to CNC output—and partnerships like the one with Rockwell Automation for edge-to-cloud manufacturing execution system integration. Risks include tariff escalations and raw material inflation, with steel up 15% quarter-over-quarter, but our 45% gross margins provide buffer.

Before I hand it over, let me address the impact of macroeconomic factors on our end-market demand, as this has been a key theme in our discussions with investors. Our $2.8 billion in Q3 revenue reflects a 7% year-over-year increase, but beneath that headline lies a nuanced story shaped by persistent macro headwinds and pockets of resilience.

Global industrial production, as tracked by the S&P Global PMI, averaged 49.2 in Q3—still in contractionary territory for the fourth straight quarter—putting downward pressure on capex across our customer base. Elevated interest rates, now hovering at 5.25-5.50% in the U.S. and 4.25% at the ECB, have delayed OEM projects, with our book-to-bill ratio dipping to 1.05x from 1.18x a year ago. Inventory destocking, particularly in automotive and general manufacturing, shaved about 300 basis points off our organic demand growth. Raw material inflation—steel up 8% year-over-year and copper at $4.20 per pound—has squeezed channel partner margins, leading to selective ordering. Yet, our backlog stands at a healthy $4.2 billion, up 12% sequentially, signaling underlying strength as utilization rates in key factories creep back toward 82%.

Breaking it down by end market, factory automation was our bright spot, growing 15% year-over-year to $850 million in revenue. The surge in semiconductor capex—Intel's $20 billion Ohio fab and TSMC's Arizona expansion—drove demand for our precision CNC machining centers and robotic palletizers, with order intake up 22%. We saw similar tailwinds in EV battery production, where our high-throughput laser welders captured 18% market share in North American gigafactories. Conversely, oil and gas was flat at $450 million, as Brent crude stabilizing around $82 per barrel encouraged maintenance capex but not new drilling rigs. Our subsea pump systems benefited from offshore projects in the Gulf of Mexico, but Permian Basin frac sand equipment orders softened amid efficiency gains from longer laterals.

Heavy construction and mining faced the stiffest headwinds, down 5% to $620 million. U.S. infrastructure spending under the IIJA is ramping—over $100 billion allocated through 2026—but high borrowing costs have pushed back non-residential starts by 10-15%, per Dodge Data Analytics. Globally, our earthmoving equipment like hydraulic excavators saw destocking in channel inventories, now at 110 days' supply versus our target of 90. Renewables, however, provided a 25% uplift to $280 million, fueled by the IRA's PTC extensions; our wind turbine gearboxes and solar tracker actuators are scaling with NextEra's 10 GW pipeline.

Regionally, North America, 55% of our mix, grew 9% year-over-year, buoyed by reshoring and CHIPS Act funding. Factory utilization in the Rust Belt hit 85%, driving retooling for our modular assembly lines. Europe, at 25% of revenue, contracted 3%, hammered by the energy crisis—German chemical plants at 72% utilization dragged demand for our process valves and compressors. Asia-Pacific, 15%, was mixed: China's real estate slump—new starts down 22% year-over-year—hit our concrete batching plants, but semiconductor and solar fab investments in Southeast Asia offset this, with Vietnam orders up 30%.

Strategically, we've leaned into technical initiatives to counter these macros. Our ApexEdge platform—integrating IoT sensors, AI predictive maintenance, and digital twins—has improved customer uptime by 18%, justifying premium pricing of 5-7% on new orders. We've accelerated R&D into electrification, launching 15kW brushless motors for off-highway equipment that cut fuel use by 25%, aligning with Cummins and Deere's net-zero roadmaps. Diversification is key: renewables now 12% of backlog, up from 7% in 2022, while we've de-risked China exposure to under 8% via localized production in Mexico under USMCA.

Looking forward, we see macro tailwinds emerging. Fed cuts starting in Q1 2025 could unlock $50-70 billion in delayed U.S. industrial capex, per our customer surveys. ISM new orders index ticked to 52.3 in September, a leading indicator for our Q4 pipeline.

Turning now to our operating margin performance by segment, which came in at a robust 15.8% for the quarter—up 210 basis points year-over-year and 80 basis points sequentially from Q2. This marks our strongest quarterly margin in three years, driven by a favorable product mix shift toward high-margin automation and aftermarket services, disciplined pricing actions across the board, and the early benefits from our Supply Chain Resilience Initiative, which has shaved 1.5% off variable costs through localized sourcing of critical components like high-strength steel and rare earth magnets.

Starting with our Industrial Machinery segment, which represents 35% of total revenue at $1.2 billion this quarter—up 12% year-over-year. Operating margin expanded to 16.5%, a 230 basis point improvement from 14.2% last year. This was fueled by strong demand for our precision CNC lathes and hydraulic presses, particularly in the automotive OEM space, where we're seeing reshoring tailwinds from the U.S. CHIPS Act and similar incentives in Europe. Volumes grew 8% year-over-year, but pricing drove the margin story: we implemented a 5-7% list price increase on Tier 1 equipment, with 85% pass-through, and factory utilization hit 92% at our Peoria, Illinois, and Monterrey, Mexico plants—up from 84% a year ago. North America led at 18.2% margins from IIJA infrastructure spending, while EMEA was 14.8% due to softer capex in Germany. Asia-Pacific held at 15.9%. We're accelerating our Digital Thread platform rollout, boosting mix by 2 points.

Automation Solutions delivered revenue of $950 million—up 18% year-over-year—with margins at 19.7%, up 150 basis points. Software and recurring SaaS now 28% of sales, up from 22%, driving 35%+ gross margins. Cobots and PLC systems grew 25% in units as Ford and Siemens upgrade for EV assembly. Our Edge AI Predictive Analytics suite cuts downtime by 22%. APAC hit 22.1% on semi fabs, U.S. 18.9%, EMEA 17.4% on GDPR. Targeting 21%+ in FY24 via GIDC Cloud.

Power Systems, 22% of revenue or $780 million flat year-over-year, saw margins at 12.4%, down 90 basis points from mix and turbine components. Diesel gensets for data centers up 15%, but wind gearboxes softened. Copper up 11%, hedged 60%. North America 14.2% on hyperscalers, EMEA 10.8% on Ukraine issues. Launching hydrogen-ready microturbines to lift to 14%+.

Aftermarket & Services generated $650 million—up 22% year-over-year—margins at 31.2%, up 240 basis points. Parts up 19%, services 42% of mix via APM tool for 30% faster predictions. Consistent regionally: U.S. 32.5%, EMEA 30.1%, APAC 30.8%. Bundling with new sales for 35% long-term.

In aggregate, mix shifted 3 points to Automation/Services, adding 140 basis points, plus $180 million productivity savings. SG&A down to 9.2%. For Q4, guiding 16.0-16.5%.

On supply chain constraints and component availability, we've navigated geopolitical tensions, Red Sea disruptions adding 10-15% to freight, and Ukraine inflating steel by 25-30%. Our book-to-bill is 1.3x for Q3, but lead times peaked at 22 weeks from Tier 2 shortages.

Semiconductors for PLCs/VFDs at 88% of demand, up from 65%, impacting 12% BOM. Bearings 14 weeks. Castings 95% OTIF. Delays now 7% of $2.8 billion backlog, down 61%, inventory 18 weeks.

Asia 45% sourcing: reduced China to 22%, freight $4,200/FEU. EMEA steel up 22%, shifted to Turkey 92% OTIF. North America nearshoring cuts valves 40%.

Invested $120 million in resilience: AVL up 40%, AI twins 92% accuracy, 51% foundry stake, Guadalajara assembly. Hedged 70% steel at $850/ton. Lead times to 10-12 weeks Q4.

Next, our order intake hit $2.85 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 12% sequentially, book-to-bill 1.28x, backlog $12.4 billion up 22%.

Construction 42% at $1.20 billion up 25%, book-to-bill 1.45x NA, 1.22x EMEA, IIJA and India pipeline. HX Series $180 million win, hybrid backhoes.

Mining 28% $800 million up 14%, 1.35x, copper/iron firm. NA $420 million, MT795AC $250 million. IntelliMine cuts downtime 18%.

Agriculture 18% $510 million up 9%, 1.15x. AGX-500 $120 million, FarmConnect up 35% telematics.

Other 12% $340 million up 22%, 1.40x on LNG/power.

Now, on operating margin guidance: Q4 14.0-15.0%, up 100-200 bps from Q3's 13.1%. Mix to CNC/automation +150 bps, IoT OEE 88%, pricing 4-6%, aftermarket 28%. NA 18-20%, Europe 12-13%, APAC EV 22%. FY24 raised to 14.5-15.5%, +250 bps YoY, via Monterrey ramp, servitization 40% attach.

Finally, our dividend policy targets 35-45% payout, up 8% to $0.58 quarterly, $2.32 annualized, 2.7% yield vs. sector 1.8%. Payout 38%, FCF 1.7x, $1.2 billion OCF YTD. Paired with $500 million buybacks. 7-10% CAGR ahead on 18% margins, electrification.

Now, I'll hand over to Lisa for an operational update.

Lisa Patel (COO):
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've been focused on optimizing our supply chain, improving manufacturing efficiency to 92% utilization in key plants, and enhancing customer service through data analytics and IoT for predictive maintenance. We're leveraging these tools to drive operational excellence, including digital twins and lean initiatives that delivered $180 million in savings. We are also investing in employee training and development to build a highly skilled workforce, supporting our capacity ramps in Mexico and South Carolina.

I'll turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Raj Singh, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Raj Singh (CTO):
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. We are investing in research and development in areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and the Internet of Things. We are developing solutions to improve predictive maintenance—cutting downtime by up to 22%—and optimize our customers' operations via platforms like ApexEdge and TechStack 3.0. Our new ApexFlex EV Press is exceeding expectations, with $250 million in orders already and overall equipment effectiveness averaging 92%, delivering 25% higher throughput for EV assembly.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star then 1. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you discuss the trends you are seeing in automation spending?

Dr. Raj Singh:
Good morning, Emily. Automation spending remains a standout, growing 15-18% year-over-year, particularly in semiconductors and EV battery production. CHIPS Act expansions at TSMC and Intel have driven 22% order growth for our CNC centers and palletizers, while North American gigafactories favor our laser welders and cobots. Our Edge AI suite and IoT integration are key differentiators, delivering 3x ROI via 22% downtime reductions. We expect sustained momentum into 2025 as reshoring accelerates, with book-to-bill over 1.2x in this segment.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee (Goldman Sachs):
What is your strategy for managing inflation and rising input costs?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, David. We've managed inflation effectively through 4-6% pricing pass-through on 85% of backlog, hedging 70% of steel at $850 per ton versus spot $1,050, and dynamic clauses on copper/nickel. Localized sourcing and VAVE recovered 60% of 11% copper hikes, while productivity from IoT shaved 1.5-2% off variables. Gross margins held at 44.5% despite 8-15% input rises. Our 45% buffer and aftermarket 31% margins provide resilience—we're guiding stable Q4 margins ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sophia Rodriguez (Morgan Stanley):
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce your carbon footprint?

John Ramirez:
Thanks, Sophia. Sustainability is core to our strategy. Our equipment cuts energy use by 30% via VFDs and cryogenic tech, qualifying for IRA credits. We've launched 15kW brushless motors reducing fuel 25%, hybrid backhoes, and hydrogen-ready microturbines. Renewables now 12% backlog, up from 7%, with Vestas $180 million deal. Internally, digital twins optimize our factories to 92% OEE, and we're targeting net-zero aligned with customer roadmaps like Cummins and Deere. Progress includes 18% uptime gains via predictive tools.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

John Ramirez:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Industrial Equipment. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
